1.solution: Let \(\vec{A}+\vec{B}=\vec{C}\), with angle \(\theta\) between \(\vec{A}\) and \(\vec{B}\). When \(\vec{B}\) is doubled, the new resultant \(\vec{C_1}=\vec{A}+2\vec{B}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{A}\). The component of \(\vec{A}+2\vec{B}\) along \(\vec{A}\) must vanish: \(A+2B\cos\theta=0\), so \(A=-2B\cos\theta\). Now \(C^2=A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta\). Note \(2AB\cos\theta=A\cdot(2B\cos\theta)=A\cdot(-A)=-A^2\). Hence \(C^2=A^2+B^2-A^2=B^2\), giving \(C=B\).

2.solution: For a real, inverted image twice the object size, magnification \(m=\dfrac{v}{u}=-2\), so \(v=-2u\). Lens formula: \(\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{v}-\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{-2u}-\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{-3}{2u}\). With \(f=\dfrac{1}{3}\,m\): \(u=-\dfrac{3}{2}f=-\dfrac{3}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{3}=-0.5\,m\). The object distance is \(0.5\,m\).

3.solution: A tuning fork resonates only with a fork whose frequency is an integral multiple (harmonic) of its own. \(512=2\times256\) and \(768=3\times256\) are harmonics, and \(256\,Hz\) is identical. But \(754\,Hz\) is not an integral multiple of \(256\,Hz\), so it will not resonate with the \(256\,Hz\) fork.

4.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
4.solution: A charge rotating once per second is an effective current \(I=\dfrac{q}{t}=1000e\). The field at the centre of the circular path is \(B=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}\). Given \(B=x\mu_0\): \(x\mu_0=\dfrac{\mu_0(1000e)}{2r}\), so \(r=\dfrac{1000e}{2x}=\dfrac{1000\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{2\times(2\times10^{-16})}=\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-16}}{4\times10^{-16}}=0.4\,m\).

5.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
5.solution: Frequency \(f=\dfrac{x}{t}\) and radius \(r=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\,m\). Tangential velocity \(v=\omega r=2\pi f r=2\pi\times\dfrac{x}{t}\times\dfrac{\pi}{2}=\dfrac{\pi^2 x}{t}\).

6.solution: In Bohr's model \(v_n\propto\dfrac{1}{n}\) and \(r_n\propto n^2\). The frequency of revolution \(f=\dfrac{v_n}{2\pi r_n}\propto\dfrac{1/n}{n^2}=\dfrac{1}{n^3}\). Hence \(f\) is inversely proportional to \(n^3\).

7.solution: Rise in temperature \(\Delta T=T_2-T_1=82.3-38.6=43.7^{\circ}C\). For a difference, absolute errors add: \(\Delta(\delta T)=0.2+0.3=0.5\). Hence \(\Delta T=(43.7\pm0.5)^{\circ}C\).

8.subtopic: Viscosity, Stokes' Law, Terminal Velocity, and Reynolds
8.solution: Terminal velocity \(v\propto r^2\). For the small drops \(V\propto r^2\) and for the big drop \(v_b\propto R^2\). Dividing: \(\dfrac{v_b}{V}=\dfrac{R^2}{r^2}\), so \(v_b=\dfrac{VR^2}{r^2}\).
8.stemOverride: \(n\) small water drops of the same size (radius \(r\)) fall through air with constant terminal velocity \(V\). They coalesce to form a big drop of radius \(R\). The terminal velocity of the big drop is
8.note: Stem and options were garbled by extraction (stray $ and broken delimiters); reconstructed. Answer A unchanged.

9.solution: For a spring-mass system \(T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}\), so \(\dfrac{m}{k}=\dfrac{T^2}{4\pi^2}=\dfrac{36}{4\pi^2}=\dfrac{9}{\pi^2}\). At rest, \(mg=kx\), so the static stretch \(x=\dfrac{m}{k}g=\dfrac{9}{\pi^2}\times\pi^2=9\,m\) (using \(g=\pi^2=10\)).

11.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
11.solution: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes the change in flux that produces it. This opposition requires work to be done against the induced effect, which is exactly what conserves energy. Thus Lenz's law in induction is a direct consequence of the conservation of energy.

12.solution: From the circuit: A passes through a NOT gate giving \(X=\overline{A}\); B and C pass through a NAND gate giving \(Z=\overline{B\cdot C}\); X and Z feed an OR gate: \(Y=\overline{A}+\overline{B\cdot C}\). When all inputs are LOW \((A=B=C=0)\): \(Y=1+1=1\). When all inputs are HIGH \((A=B=C=1)\): \(Y=0+0=0\). Hence the outputs are \((1,0)\).
12.note: Figure: A->NOT, (B,C)->NAND, both into OR gate. AK solution mis-modelled the NAND as B-bar AND C but still reached the correct (1,0).

13.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
13.solution: Average kinetic energy of a molecule \(\propto T\). Therefore \(\dfrac{(KE)_B}{(KE)_A}=\dfrac{T_B}{T_A}=\dfrac{420}{350}=\dfrac{6}{5}\), i.e. \(6:5\).

14.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
14.solution: In S.H.M. the restoring force \(F=-m\omega^2 y\), so force and displacement are exactly out of phase (phase difference \(\pi\)). The given displacement-time graph rises to a positive peak first; the force-time graph must therefore start by going negative (the inverted curve). This is option (C).
14.note: Given displacement graph (image4) rises first; options (image5-8): (A) declining line, (B) rising line, (C) sine starting downward (out of phase), (D) sine starting upward (in phase). Correct = (C), inverted/out of phase with displacement.

15.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
15.solution: Phase angle \(\phi=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{X_L}{R}\right)=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi f L}{R}\right)\). Here \(2\pi f L=2\pi\times\dfrac{150}{\pi}\times1.5=450\,\Omega\). So \(\phi=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{450}{450}\right)=\tan^{-1}(1)\).

16.solution: The sphere enters the liquid with speed \(u=\sqrt{2gh}\). Inside the liquid (\(\sigma>\rho\)) the net upward force gives deceleration \(a=\dfrac{(\sigma-\rho)g}{\rho}\). It stops when \(v=0\): \(0=u^2-2aH\), so \(H=\dfrac{u^2}{2a}=\dfrac{2gh}{2\,(\sigma-\rho)g/\rho}=\dfrac{h\rho}{\sigma-\rho}\). The intended option is \(\dfrac{h\rho}{(\rho-\sigma)}\) (option D, denominator written with reversed sign; magnitude \(=\dfrac{h\rho}{\sigma-\rho}\)).
16.note: Magnitude of depth is h*rho/(sigma-rho); option D writes the denominator as (rho-sigma). D is the intended answer despite the sign typo in the printed option.

17.solution: Thermal resistances in series: \(R_1=\dfrac{x}{KA}\), \(R_2=\dfrac{4x}{2KA}=\dfrac{2x}{KA}\), so \(R_{eq}=\dfrac{3x}{KA}\). Rate of heat flow \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=\dfrac{T_2-T_1}{R_{eq}}=\dfrac{KA(T_2-T_1)}{3x}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{A(T_2-T_1)K}{x}\right]\). Hence \(f=\dfrac{1}{3}\).

18.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
18.solution: A pipe closed at one end has only odd harmonics. Its overtones are \(3n, 5n, 7n\) (first, second, third overtones), where \(n\) is the fundamental. Given \(3n+5n+7n=15n=3930\), so \(n=262\,Hz\).

19.note: Option units are printed as Wb (should be N m^2/C); answer magnitude A is correct.

20.subtopic: Projectile Motion — Range, Height, and Time of Flight
20.solution: Initial KE \(E=\dfrac{1}{2}mu^2\). At the highest point only the horizontal velocity \(u\cos\theta\) remains. So KE there \(=\dfrac{1}{2}m(u\cos\theta)^2=\dfrac{1}{2}mu^2\cos^2\theta=E\cos^2\theta\).

21.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
21.solution: Intensity \(I=4I_0\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{2}\) where \(\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\,\Delta x\). For \(\Delta x=\dfrac{\lambda}{4}\), \(\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(I=4I_0\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4}=2I_0=\dfrac{K}{2}\), giving \(K=4I_0\). For \(\Delta x=\lambda\), \(\phi=2\pi\), so \(I=4I_0\cos^2\pi=4I_0=K\).

22.subtopic: Magnetisation, Susceptibility, Permeability, and B-H-M Relations
22.solution: The net magnetic field inside a material is the sum of the applied field and the field due to magnetisation: \(B=\mu_0(H+M)\).

23.solution: Impulse = change in momentum = area under the F-t graph. From the graph, \(F=8\,N\) for \(0\) to \(0.5\,s\) and \(F=4\,N\) for \(0.5\) to \(1.0\,s\). Area \(=8\times0.5+4\times0.5=4+2=6\,N\cdot s\). So \(mv=6\), \(v=\dfrac{6}{3}=2\,m/s\).
23.note: Figure (image9): step F-t graph, 8 N for 0-0.5 s then 4 N for 0.5-1.0 s.

24.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
24.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
24.solution: For an accelerated electron, \(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{V}}\). Hence \(\dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda}=\sqrt{\dfrac{V}{9V}}=\dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(\lambda_2=\dfrac{\lambda}{3}\).

25.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
25.solution: Maximum tension \(T_{max}=3.7\,kg\,wt=3.7\times10=37\,N\). At the lowest point of a vertical circle the tension is maximum: \(T_{max}=mg+m\omega^2 r\). With \(m=0.5\,kg\), \(r=4\,m\): \(37=0.5\times10+0.5\times\omega^2\times4=5+2\omega^2\). So \(2\omega^2=32\), \(\omega^2=16\), \(\omega=4\,rad/s\).

26.subtopic: Viscosity, Stokes' Law, Terminal Velocity, and Reynolds
26.solution: For steady (laminar) flow with velocity increasing linearly from the bed, \(\dfrac{v}{h}\) is constant: \(\dfrac{v_A}{h_A}=\dfrac{v_B}{h_B}\). With \(v_A=12\,cm/s\), \(h_A=40\,cm\), \(h_B=90\,cm\): \(v_B=v_A\times\dfrac{h_B}{h_A}=12\times\dfrac{90}{40}=27\,cm/s\).
26.stemOverride: Water is flowing steadily in a river. A and B are the two layers of water at heights 40 cm and 90 cm from the bottom. The velocity of the layer A is \(12\,cm/s\). The velocity of the layer B is
26.note: Stem velocity of layer A printed as '2 cm/s' is an extraction typo (dropped digit). The AK solution itself uses 12 cm/s, which gives 27 cm/s = option C. Stem corrected to 12 cm/s.

27.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
27.solution: Wavelength \(\lambda=\dfrac{v}{f}=\dfrac{336}{400}=0.84\,m\). A phase difference of \(60^{\circ}\) corresponds to a path difference \(\dfrac{60}{360}\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda}{6}\). So separation \(=\dfrac{0.84}{6}=0.14\,m\).
27.stemOverride: A progressive wave of frequency 400 Hz is travelling with velocity \(336\,m/s\). How far apart are the two points on a wave which are \(60^{\circ}\) out of phase?
27.note: Stem velocity printed as '36 m/s' is an extraction typo (dropped digit). The AK solution uses 336 m/s, which gives 0.14 m = option B. Stem corrected to 336 m/s.

28.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge

29.solution: Bohr quantisation: \(mvR=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\) ... (i). For motion in a transverse field, \(qvB=\dfrac{mv^2}{R}\Rightarrow mvR=\dfrac{qBR^2}{1}\)... eliminating, from (i) \(R=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi mv}\). Using \(qvB=\dfrac{mv^2}{R}\Rightarrow qBR=mv\), combine with (i): \(qBR\cdot R=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\Rightarrow qBR^2=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\). Energy \(E=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2=\dfrac{1}{2}qBvR\). Since \(mv=qBR\) and \(mvR=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\Rightarrow vR=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi m}\). Thus \(E=\dfrac{1}{2}qB\,vR=\dfrac{1}{2}qB\cdot\dfrac{nh}{2\pi m}=\dfrac{nqBh}{4\pi m}\). For \(n=2\): \(E=\dfrac{qBh}{2\pi m}\).

30.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
30.solution: For a body, \(a+r+t_r=1\) (absorption + reflection + transmission coefficients). So \(t_r=1-(0.77+0.17)=0.06\). Heat transmitted \(=t_r\times Q=0.06\times250=15\,kcal\).

31.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
31.solution: First minimum from centre: \(y_1=\dfrac{\lambda D}{a}\). Distance between the two first minima on either side: \(2y_1=\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}\). So \(1\times10^{-2}=\dfrac{2\lambda\times2}{0.2\times10^{-3}}\), giving \(\lambda=\dfrac{(1\times10^{-2})(0.2\times10^{-3})}{4}=5\times10^{-7}\,m=5000\,\text{ angstrom}\).

32.solution: \(\dfrac{L}{R}\) has the unit \(\dfrac{\text{henry}}{\text{ohm}}\). The time constant of an LR circuit is \(\tau=\dfrac{L}{R}\), which has the SI unit of second.

33.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
33.solution: Impedance \(Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_L^2}=\sqrt{R^2+3R^2}=2R\). Average power \(P=\dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt2}\cdot\dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt2 Z}\cdot\cos\phi\) with \(\cos\phi=\dfrac{R}{Z}=\dfrac{1}{2}\). So \(P=\dfrac{E_0^2}{2(2R)}\times\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{E_0^2}{8R}\).

34.solution: Force \(F=qE\), acceleration \(a=\dfrac{qE}{m}\), starting from rest \(v=at=\dfrac{qEt}{m}\). KE \(=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2=\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\dfrac{qEt}{m}\right)^2=\dfrac{q^2E^2t^2}{2m}\).

35.solution: Internal resistance \(r=R\left(\dfrac{l}{l_1}-1\right)\), where \(l\) is the open-circuit balancing length. So \(5\left(\dfrac{l}{250}-1\right)=20\left(\dfrac{l}{400}-1\right)\). This gives \(\dfrac{l}{50}-5=\dfrac{l}{20}-20\Rightarrow15=\dfrac{3l}{100}\Rightarrow l=500\,cm\). Then \(r=5\left(\dfrac{500}{250}-1\right)=5\,\Omega\).

36.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
36.solution: Sliding (no rotation): \(V=\sqrt{2gh}\). Rolling: \(v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1+K^2/R^2}}\). For a ring \(K^2/R^2=1\), so \(v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{2}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2gh}}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{V}{\sqrt2}\).

37.solution: Initial parallel combination: \(C_i=C+C=2C\). After filling one capacitor with dielectric \(K\): \(C_f=C+KC=C(1+K)\). Change \(\Delta C=C(1+K)-2C=C(K-1)\).

38.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
38.solution: Using \(PV=nRT\) at constant T,V: before, \(n_1=\dfrac{PV}{RT}\); after, \(n_2=\dfrac{P'V}{RT}\). Moles leaked \(=n_1-n_2=\dfrac{V}{RT}(P-P')\).
38.note: Stem uses P' for the reduced pressure (printed as 'P' twice due to extraction); option B = V/RT (P - P').

39.subtopic: Gravitational PE, Escape Velocity, and Energy
39.solution: Escape velocity \(v_e=\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}\) depends on \(G\), the mass \(M\) of the earth and its radius \(R\), but not on the mass of the projected object.

40.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
40.solution: In an unbiased p-n junction, diffusion leaves the depletion region with negative ions on the p-side and positive ions on the n-side, creating a built-in field directed from the n-side to the p-side. The n-side is at higher potential than the p-side.

41.subtopic: Kinetic Theory — Pressure, RMS Speed, and Temperature

42.subtopic: Ohm's Law, Cells, EMF, and Internal Resistance
42.solution: Two equal cells in series: \(I=\dfrac{2E}{R+r_1+r_2}\). Terminal p.d. across cell \(E_1\): \(V_1=E-Ir_1=0\). So \(E=\dfrac{2E\,r_1}{R+r_1+r_2}\Rightarrow R+r_1+r_2=2r_1\Rightarrow R=r_1-r_2\).

43.subtopic: SHM Energy — Kinetic, Potential, and Total
43.solution: Total energy \(E=\dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\) with amplitude \(A\) fixed. For a pendulum \(\omega^2=\dfrac{g}{l}\), so \(E\propto\dfrac{1}{l}\). Reducing \(l\) to \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) makes \(E\) three times larger.

44.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
44.subtopic: Force on Current-Carrying Conductor and Parallel Wires
44.solution: Force per length between parallel wires \(F\propto\dfrac{I_1 I_2}{d}\). Initially attractive (same direction): \(F=k\dfrac{I_1 I_2}{d}\). After increasing separation to \(3d\) the force becomes repulsive of magnitude \(\dfrac{2}{3}F\): \(\dfrac{2}{3}\,k\dfrac{I_1 I_2}{d}=k\dfrac{I_1' I_2}{3d}\). Solving for the magnitude: \(|I_1'|=2I_1\). A repulsive force requires the currents to be antiparallel, i.e. the direction is reversed. So the current must be made twice and reversed.

45.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain

46.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
46.solution: At constant pressure \(\Delta Q=nC_p\Delta T\), \(\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T\). Fraction into internal energy \(\dfrac{\Delta U}{\Delta Q}=\dfrac{C_v}{C_p}=\dfrac{1}{\gamma}\). For a monoatomic gas \(\gamma=\dfrac{5}{3}\), so \(\dfrac{\Delta U}{\Delta Q}=\dfrac{3}{5}=60\%\) (A) and external work \(=40\%\) (B). Hence \(A:B=60:40=3:2\).

47.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
47.solution: LR circuit power factor \(X_1=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+X_L^2}}=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+9R^2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\). Adding \(X_C=R\) gives an LCR circuit: \(X_2=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}}=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+(3R-R)^2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\). Ratio \(\dfrac{X_1}{X_2}=\dfrac{1/\sqrt{10}}{1/\sqrt5}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\), i.e. \(1:\sqrt2\).

48.solution: On a sonometer \(f\propto\dfrac{1}{l}\). The shorter length (0.69 m) gives the higher frequency. Beat frequency \(f_2-f_1=6\). With \(\dfrac{f_1}{f_2}=\dfrac{l_2}{l_1}=\dfrac{0.69}{0.70}\), solving \(f_1\cdot0.70=f_2\cdot0.69\) with \(f_2-f_1=6\) gives \(f_1=414\,Hz\) and \(f_2=420\,Hz\).

49.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
49.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
49.stemOverride: The maximum velocity of the photoelectrons emitted by a metal surface is \(9\times10^{5}\,m/s\). The value of ratio of charge (e) to mass (m) of the photoelectron is \(1.8\times10^{11}\,C/kg\). The value of stopping potential in volt is
49.note: Stem maximum velocity printed as 'x10^5 m/s' missing the coefficient; AK solution uses 9x10^5 m/s giving 2.25 V = option B. Stem corrected.

50.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
50.solution: A point exactly in front of one slit is at \(y=\dfrac{d}{2}\). The \(n\)th minimum lies at \(y_n=\dfrac{(2n-1)\lambda D}{2d}\). For the 3rd minimum \((n=3)\): \(\dfrac{d}{2}=\dfrac{5\lambda D}{2d}\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac{d^2}{5D}\). For the 1st minimum \((n=1)\) at the same point: \(\dfrac{d}{2}=\dfrac{\lambda' D}{2d}\Rightarrow\lambda'=\dfrac{d^2}{D}=5\lambda\). Required change \(\Delta\lambda=\lambda'-\lambda=4\lambda\).
